items.title: What is Power BI? (10 min beginner)
items.creator: various

items.title: Who reads this dashboard?
items.body: Imagine the Sample Superstore is a real retailer. Three people open this dashboard every Monday: the CEO, the regional VP, the category manager. Write 3 KPIs each persona would care about most. 9 KPIs total. We'll use this to pick the right 4 for the dashboard.

items.title: Power BI Desktop (free)
items.why: Click 'Open' to install from Microsoft Store. Windows only. If you don't have Windows, see the Mac note in this week's intro.

items.title: Power BI Desktop install + interface tour (15 min)
items.creator: various

items.title: Install + open
items.body:
STEP 1 — Install Power BI Desktop from the card above (Microsoft Store, free).
  Mac users: install Windows in a VirtualBox VM (free) or use app.powerbi.com directly with reduced features.

STEP 2 — Open Power BI Desktop.
  YOU SHOULD SEE: a welcome page. Click 'Get data' → 'Excel workbook'.

STEP 3 — Download Sample Superstore (same file as Data Analysis Week 1) from this URL:
  https://community.tableau.com/s/question/0D54T00000CWeX8SAL/sample-superstore-sales-excelxls
  Save it to your Desktop in a folder called superstore-bi.

STEP 4 — Import.
  In Power BI Desktop, point Get Data to your Sample - Superstore.xls.
  Check Orders, Returns, People. Click Transform Data → Power Query opens.

days.title: Clean in Power Query
days.summary: Today we clean the data BEFORE we model.

items.title: Power Query for beginners — Guy in a Cube
items.creator: Guy in a Cube

items.title: Power Query clean
items.body:
Power Query is open from yesterday. You see 3 tables on the left.

STEP 1 — Click the Orders table.

STEP 2 — Set column types.
  Click Order Date column → change type to Date.
  Click Ship Date column → Date.
  Click Sales, Profit, Discount → Decimal Number.

STEP 3 — Remove Row ID.
  Right-click Row ID column → Remove.

STEP 4 — Add Profit Margin column.
  Add Column tab → Custom Column.
  Name: Margin
  Formula: = [Profit] / [Sales]
  OK. Set the new column type to Percentage.

STEP 5 — Rename Sub-Category to Subcategory (consistency).
  Right-click → Rename.

STEP 6 — Click 'Close & Apply' (top left).
  Power BI Desktop reopens with your data loaded.

STEP 7 — Save the file.
  File → Save As → superstore.pbix → in your superstore-bi folder.

days.title: Build a date dimension table
days.summary: BI works best with a separate calendar table. Today we make one.

items.title: Create DimDate
items.body:
STEP 1 — In Power BI Desktop, Modeling tab → New table.

STEP 2 — In the formula bar, type:
      DimDate = CALENDAR(DATE(2020,1,1), DATE(2024,12,31))
  Press Enter.
  YOU SHOULD SEE: a new table called DimDate with one column 'Date'.

STEP 3 — Add columns. With DimDate selected, Modeling tab → New column.
      Year = YEAR(DimDate[Date])
  New column again:
      Month = FORMAT(DimDate[Date], "MMM")
  New column:
      Quarter = "Q" & QUARTER(DimDate[Date])

STEP 4 — Connect to Orders.
  Click the Model view (middle icon on the left sidebar).
  Drag DimDate[Date] onto Orders[Order Date].
  YOU SHOULD SEE: a line connecting them. Cardinality should be One-to-Many.

STEP 5 — Save.

days.title: Write 6 DAX measures
days.summary: DAX = the formula language of Power BI. Today: 6 measures.

items.title: DAX measures
items.body:
STEP 1 — In Power BI Desktop, click the Orders table on the right.
  Modeling tab → New measure.

STEP 2 — Type these one at a time. After each, press Enter and Modeling → New measure again:

      Total Sales = SUM(Orders[Sales])

      Total Profit = SUM(Orders[Profit])

      Profit Margin = DIVIDE([Total Profit], [Total Sales])

      Sales LY = CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(DimDate[Date]))

      YoY Growth = DIVIDE([Total Sales] - [Sales LY], [Sales LY])

      Sales YTD = TOTALYTD([Total Sales], DimDate[Date])

STEP 3 — Test in a card.
  Click the Report view (top icon on left sidebar).
  In the Visualizations pane, click the 'Card' icon.
  Drag [Total Sales] into Fields.
  YOU SHOULD SEE: $2,297,200 (or similar) in a big card. Your first DAX measure rendered.

days.title: Build the dashboard page
days.summary: Today you arrange everything into a 1-page dashboard.

items.title: Lay it out
items.body:
STEP 1 — In Report view, you have a blank canvas. Plan the layout:
  TOP (4 cards): Total Sales | Total Profit | Profit Margin | YoY Growth
  MIDDLE LEFT: line chart of Sales over time
  MIDDLE RIGHT: bar chart of Sales by Region
  BOTTOM: matrix of Subcategory + Margin
  LEFT SIDE: date slicer

STEP 2 — 4 KPI cards.
  Click Card visual. Drag Total Sales. Resize to ~200x100. Place top-left.
  Repeat for Total Profit, Profit Margin, YoY Growth — 4 cards in a row.

STEP 3 — Line chart.
  Click Line chart. Axis = DimDate[Year-Month] (or just Date). Values = Total Sales.
  Place in middle-left, sized ~500x300.

STEP 4 — Bar chart.
  Click Clustered bar chart. Axis = Region. Values = Total Sales.
  Middle-right, ~400x300.

STEP 5 — Matrix.
  Click Matrix. Rows = Subcategory. Values = Profit Margin.
  Click the dropdown next to Margin → Conditional Formatting → Background → set up:
    > 20% green, 5-20% yellow, < 5% red.
  Place at the bottom.

STEP 6 — Date slicer.
  Click Slicer. Drag DimDate[Date]. Change type to 'Between' or 'Relative date'.
  Place on the left side.

STEP 7 — Use colors consistently. Format the canvas. Add a title at the top.
  Save.

days.title: Publish + share + GitHub
days.summary: Today the dashboard goes ONLINE with a real URL.

items.title: Power BI Service — sign up (free)
items.why: Click 'Open' to sign up. Use a work or school email if you have one. Otherwise: see Step 1 below for free Microsoft account.

items.title: Publish + push
items.body:
STEP 1 — Sign up for Power BI Service.
  Open the Power BI signup card. If it complains about your email — get a free Microsoft 365 Developer account: developer.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/dev-program. Use the email it gives you.

STEP 2 — Publish from Desktop.
  In Power BI Desktop: Home tab → Publish → My workspace.
  Wait 30-60 seconds. YOU SHOULD SEE: 'Success!' with a link.

STEP 3 — Open the published report.
  Click the link. Power BI Service opens in your browser. Your report is live.
  Copy the URL.

STEP 4 — Make it shareable (optional — requires Pro/free trial).
  In Service, click your report → Share → choose 'People with the link'.
  Or: File → Embed report → Publish to web (only if your account allows it).

STEP 5 — Push to GitHub.
  Open the 'create new repository' card. Name: superstore-bi. Public.
  In your terminal:
      cd Desktop/superstore-bi
      git init
      git add .
      git commit -m "Superstore Power BI v0.1"
      git branch -M main
      git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/superstore-bi.git
      git push -u origin main

STEP 6 — README.
  Add README.md:
      # Superstore Power BI v0.1
      Sample Superstore in Power BI with a date dimension, 6 DAX measures, 1-page dashboard.
      
      ## Live
      [Open in Power BI Service](paste-your-url-here)
      
      ## Measures
      - Total Sales
      - Total Profit
      - Profit Margin
      - Sales LY
      - YoY Growth
      - Sales YTD
      
      ## Screenshot
      ![Dashboard](dashboard.png)
  Take a screenshot of your dashboard, save as dashboard.png in the repo.
  Push again.

PASS CRITERIA — Superstore BI v0.1 ships when:
  ☐ superstore.pbix saved locally
  ☐ DimDate table connected to Orders[Order Date]
  ☐ 6 DAX measures created and working
  ☐ 1-page dashboard with 4 cards + 2 charts + matrix + slicer
  ☐ Published to Power BI Service
  ☐ Public GitHub repo named superstore-bi with .pbix + screenshot + README
